thread:
anya: FYI — customer reported tool responses getting attached to the wrong user request after the 13:22 deploy. Happens when two tools are invoked in parallel from the same chat turn. Repro below.

mike: Which tools? any example payload?

anya: In this case it's a two-tool fanout: call `web_search` and `structured_db` in parallel. We see `tool_result` for search end up mapped to the DB call on the client side.

sean: Do we have logs showing correlation ids?

anya: Yes. Server logs show two requests with the same `request_id` (expected) but different `call_id`. However the response routing layer logs only one `call_id` forwarded to the fanout worker. Snippet: 

```
INFO 2026-02-09T13:22:10Z request_id=rid_8a1 call_id=c_1 dispatch=fanout queued
INFO 2026-02-09T13:22:10Z request_id=rid_8a1 call_id=c_2 dispatch=fanout queued
INFO 2026-02-09T13:22:10Z request_id=rid_8a1 call_id=c_1 worker=kvbatch assigned
INFO 2026-02-09T13:22:10Z request_id=rid_8a1 call_id=c_1 worker=kvbatch complete -> emit result(c_1)
INFO 2026-02-09T13:22:10Z request_id=rid_8a1 worker=kvbatch emit result(call_ref=c_1)
```

anya: Notice `c_2` never assigned in the worker logs — but the client reports two responses. On the client side the second response was labelled `tool_result[web_search]` even though `c_1` came from DB.

alice: Could this be a hashing/collision in the KV-batch packing? We recently changed the prefix key to `req:<request_id>` instead of `req:<request_id>:<call_id>` to optimize storage.

mike: That sounds likely. If the worker reads `req:rid_8a1` and iterates results it might mix up call-level metadata. Any schema validation errors?

anya: We also saw a schema validation failure in the client for one of the results: `422 invalid_args: expected {tool,args} but got {tool_result}` — but that was intermittent. Full client debug: 

```
ClientRequest: {
  request_id: "rid_8a1",
  calls: [
    {call_id: "c_1", tool: "structured_db", args: {...}},
    {call_id: "c_2", tool: "web_search", args: {...}}
  ]
}
ClientReceived:
  - tool_result(call_ref=c_1, tool=web_search, result=...)
  - tool_result(call_ref=c_2, tool=structured_db, result=...)
```

sean: So the call_refs are misaligned. Could be when we coalesce the two tool outputs into a single list in the persistence layer we lose the call_id pairing. The recent change to `req:<request_id>` key would cause exactly that.

alice: Repro steps I ran on staging: 1) send a single chat turn that fans out 3 tool calls concurrently; 2) inspect worker kvbatch writes; 3) intentionally delay web_search long-poll to force ordering. Outcome: results returned in different order but the call_ids in the response map were shuffled.

mike: Workaround for customers: serialize tool calls or include unique correlation in the tool args as a stopgap (e.g., `args.__call_tag`). But we should fix root cause.

anya: Customer is on Dedicated, hit this twice in prod since the deploy. They've opened a P1. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5152 — included logs and client repro.

ops-bot: P1 incident created INF-5152. Pager notified: oncall@redwood.dev

sean: Proposed fix: revert prefix change and reintroduce call-level namespace: `req:<request_id>:<call_id>` for per-call intermediate results. Also add server-side assert: if multiple call_ids present for a request, do not collapse into a single list without preserving call_id metadata.

alice: Add unit test that simulates concurrent fanout with identical request_id and asserts stable mapping. Also add an integration test that runs kvbatch worker with race injection (sleep) to reproduce.

mike: Additional improvement: include `call_id` in the external response envelope (we already include it but let's make it mandatory in the formatter) and bump schema version to 2.1 so clients can detect mismatches: `response.v=2.1`. If mismatch, client should log and drop the problematic tool result rather than map incorrectly.

anya: For immediate mitigation I'm enabling a temporary safety check on Dedicated tenants — if the vm sees >1 concurrent tool calls for same request it will route them to isolated workers instead of packing. Rolling this to prod now.

alice: After hotfix let's run a small canary on three customer requests and verify no mis-association for 24h.

mike: Notes for support reply: apologize, explain root cause (kv packing key change introduced call-level collapse), give workaround and ETA for fix (revert + tests + canary = ~6 hrs), include remediation steps and ticket link. Keep customer updated every 2 hours.

anya: I'll draft the customer message and post here for review.

alice: Thanks. logging/tracing follow-up: add a `call_bundle_hash` field to worker logs so we can quickly detect future misbundling.

sean: Follow-up action items:
- alice: revert key prefix and add tests (high)
- mike: add response schema guard and client compat bump (medium)
- anya: customer comms + canary monitor (high)
- ops-bot: keep incident open and continue paging until 24h clean canary

anya: Drafted reply: "We're sorry — we identified a bug introduced in a recent storage optimization that caused per-call IDs to be stripped when multiple tools were packed under the same request key. We have an immediate mitigation in place and a code revert + tests deploying. We'll follow up with status updates every 2 hours."

mike: LGTM. post the draft to the ticket and send initial email.

anya: Sending now. Closing thread for updates to happen in INF-5152. :white_check_mark:
